title: Linking Words in Writing
text:
Linking words help readers follow the ideas in a text. Some connectors add information, such as 'also' and 'moreover'. Others show contrast, such as 'however' and 'although'. Because writers use these words, readers can understand how one idea relates to another.

Students often avoid connectors because they seem difficult. However, using them makes writing sound more natural and organized. For example, 'therefore' shows a result, and 'in addition' introduces another point. Therefore, practicing connectors every day can improve both reading and writing.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do linking words help readers do?
options: Follow the ideas in a text

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, why do students often avoid connectors?
options: They are only used in speech

questions.text: What can be inferred about writers who use connectors well?
options: Their texts are easier to follow

paragraph_translations: Las palabras de enlace ayudan a los lectores a seguir las ideas de un texto. Algunos conectores añaden información, como 'also' y 'moreover'. Otros muestran contraste, como 'however' y 'although'. Como los escritores usan estas palabras, los lectores pueden entender cómo se relaciona una idea con otra.

Los estudiantes a menudo evitan los conectores porque parecen difíciles. Sin embargo, usarlos hace que la escritura suene más natural y organizada. Por ejemplo, 'therefore' indica un resultado, y 'in addition' introduce otro punto. Por lo tanto, practicar los conectores todos los días puede mejorar tanto la lectura como la escritura.
